Title: 'Transporter' held with RM739,200 worth of smuggled cigarettes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 54-year-old local man who worked as a "transporter" for a Bangladeshi man was arrested with 1,350 cartons of smuggled cigarettes worth RM739,200 in Kampung Subang Baru.
The suspect received RM5,000 a month to distribute untaxed cigarettes in the local market.
In the 8am Op Taring Alpha 1 raid, a Bukit Aman police team also seized a Toyota Alphard, bringing the total value of the seizure to RM820,200.
Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation (WCB/PSK) commander of the Federal Internal Security and Public Order Department senior assistant commissioner Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the raid followed intelligence gathering and continuous monitoring of the syndicate.
He said the suspect was believed to be working as a cigarette transporter for about two years in return for the monthly payment.
"Initial interrogation found that the suspect claimed to have been involved in transporting cigarettes for about two years and received RM5,000 a month to distribute untaxed cigarettes.
"The suspect also claimed that he received instructions from a Bangladeshi man to distribute the cigarettes," he said.
Zaki said the suspect and all seized items were handed over to the Sungai Buloh district police headquarters for further investigation under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967.
He said police would continue enforcement efforts to identify and disrupt networks involved in supplying, storing, transporting and distributing untaxed goods.
"From Jan 1 to Sept 30 this year, Bukit Aman conducted 268 raids nationwide, resulting in the arrest of 455 individuals for various offences.
"During the same period, the total value of seizures was estimated at RM330,695,346.76," he said.

Title: Three houses in Sungai Petani village hit by mudslide
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: Three houses in Kampung Serukam here were affected by a mudslide following heavy rain this afternoon.
The incident is believed to have occurred after heavy rain began at 12.30 pm, causing a collapse at a nearby housing project site, before water and mud flowed into residents' homes.
One of the victims, Siti Aishah Hassan, 44, said her parents-in-law's house was inundated with water to a depth of about 0.5 metres.
She said both of them were already moved to a safe location before the incident as they had suffered strokes.
"I cannot imagine what would have happened if my parents-in-law had been in the house. The heavy rain caused the water to flow strongly and rapidly, and it rose within a very short time.
[[nid:1544917]]
"Household furnishings and electrical appliances, including the refrigerator and washing machine, were overturned, while other belongings were scattered. The inside of the house was also covered in mud," she told reporters.
She said her brother-in-law, Rashid Khamis, 44, who was asleep in the lower part of the house, also managed to save himself after realising that water and mud had entered the house.
Meanwhile, Scientex SP Astana project site supervisor Mohd Haniff Ramli said three houses were affected in the incident, including two located within the project site.
"About a year ago, a similar incident also occurred. We sent a team to clean the affected houses and also cleared the road.
[[nid:1544916]]
"For now, the residents' houses are being cleaned. After this, we will assess the damage for further action," he said.
It is understood that the affected residents living within the project site had been informed of a proposal to relocate them to another location, but the matter is still being negotiated between both parties.
The housing project is currently in the earthworks and construction phase. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hulu Selangor roads to close in stages for LTdL stage 5 on Oct 1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Several roads in Hulu Selangor will be closed in stages from 11 am tomorrow to make way for Stage 5 of the Le Tour de Langkawi (LTdL) 2026 cycling race.
Hulu Selangor police chief superintendent M Manimaran said the road closures would involve routes from KM79 of Jalan Kuala Lumpur-Ipoh at the Muallim district border, Ulu Bernam-Kalumpang-Kerling-Kuala Kubu Baru-Pekan Batang Kali to the Gohtong Jaya Roundabout.
"As such, road users are advised to use alternative routes, namely Serendah-Sungai Choh-Bukit Beruntung-Bukit Beruntung Toll-North-South Expressway-Tanjung Malim Toll; Batang Kali-Hulu Yam Bharu-Pekan Hulu Yam-Hulu Yam Lama-Serendah; and Batang Kali-Hulu Yam Bharu-Sungai Tua-Middle Ring Road 2-Gombak Toll-Genting Highlands," he said in a statement.
Manimaran said the road closures are expected to end at 1 pm, depending on the movement and routes taken by the riders.
He said the road closures were to ensure the safety of the race participants and road users, facilitate the smooth running of the event and reduce the risk of traffic congestion throughout the race.
"Members of the public, particularly road users, are advised to comply with traffic directions and controls by the personnel on duty, plan their journeys in advance, use alternative routes and give their full cooperation throughout the road closures," he added.

Title: MACC proposes governance improvements for Felda, two subsidiaries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has proposed governance improvements to the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and two of its subsidiaries to strengthen the management of two projects under the agency.
In a statement, MACC said the subsidiaries involved were FIC Supplies Sdn Bhd (FIC Supplies) and FIC Integrated Property Management (FIC IPM).
The recommendations were put forward by MACC's Governance Investigation Division (BPT) to enhance governance in the implementation of the Agro Park (Commercial) Project and the Cattle Trading Pilot Project.
Among the recommendations for Felda was the restructuring of FIC IPM's role as an independent advisory panel to ensure that all views and advice provided are objective, transparent and free from conflicts of interest.
"MACC BPT also recommended that Felda strengthen its procurement and transaction management procedures by establishing specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for procurement methods involving request for proposal (RFP) and variation orders," it said.
MACC said the measures were important to ensure that the processes were carried out consistently, systematically and transparently in line with established regulations and internal controls.
The recommendations also include improving existing procedures related to FIC Supplies' sales and purchase activities to strengthen controls and governance in the company's transactions.
The proposals were presented by MACC BPT deputy director I Maznah Che Muda at Menara Felda here on Monday.
Meanwhile, Felda and its subsidiaries welcomed the recommendations to strengthen governance, transparency and integrity within the agency, while expressing their commitment to implement them in stages.
The agreement to adopt the recommendations was formalised through the Governance Improvement Report signed by Felda deputy director-general (Corporate Services) Muhammad Fitri Othman, FIC Group chief executive officer Syed Fadil Syed Sofi and MACC BPT director Datuk Mohd Zaki Hassan.

Title: US-led coalition ends mission in Iraq
Article:
BAGHDAD: A US-led coalition deployed in Iraq more than a decade ago to fight jihadists concluded its mission on Wednesday, a move celebrated by the country's leaders, but which some fear will embolden pro-Iran armed factions.
Coalition troops deployed to Iraq and Syria in 2014 to fight the Islamic State group, which had seized large swathes of territory, committing massacres and forcing thousands of women and children into slavery.
The group was defeated in Iraq in 2017 and in Syria in 2019, but coalition forces stayed on to battle the group's remnants.
The United States and Iraq agreed in 2024 to wind down the coalition's mission, and its troops withdrew gradually from bases across the country, restricting their presence to the autonomous northern Kurdistan region.
On Wednesday, the US announced the mission's formal conclusion.
"Today, the United States and our Coalition partners formally concluded Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq, consistent with the September 2024 US-Iraq joint statement and US national interests," the Pentagon said.
The US Department of Defense however added that it would "continue to provide targeted training and intelligence support to our Iraqi partners."
'SOVEREIGNTY'
The US-led coalition did not defeat IS alone.
Kurdish Peshmerga fighters played an important role, as did powerful Iraqi factions, including pro-Iran groups that have yet to disarm.
The Iraqi government, which celebrated the withdrawal, believes it will deprive Iran-backed factions of the excuse they have used to retain their arsenal.
But many Iraqis fear the pullout might embolden the pro-Iran factions further and draw the country deeper into the Middle East war.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi hailed the end of the mission as the start of a new chapter.
"A new phase has begun, defined by Iraq's sovereignty, the strength of its institutions, the readiness of its forces, unity of decision-making, and balanced partnerships with its friends," Zaidi said at a ceremony on Wednesday.
He had also declared that October 1 would be celebrated as Sovereignty Day.
It is "a national occasion that affirms the completion of Iraq's path toward sovereignty and consolidates the presence of the state and its institutions", the heads of Iraq's executive, legislative and judicial branches said on Monday.
They added that "the presence of weapons outside state authority must be addressed... in line with timelines set by the government, in a manner that strengthens state sovereignty."
INTENSIFIED ATTACKS
Zaidi, who came to power this year with the US's blessing, has vowed to reinforce the state's monopoly on arms and ensure that armed factions hand over their weapons to the state.
His government initially set September 30 as the deadline for factions to disarm, but later withdrew the time limit as talks continued to "regulate" weapons – an issue that has fuelled division and is expected to take much longer to resolve.
Kurdish military commander Sirwan Barzani expressed disquiet over the withdrawal, saying: "We have no means to protect the skies of Kurdistan."
He nonetheless told AFP that the Peshmerga forces remained prepared to confront any threats, stating that their "capabilities and experience have improved significantly thanks to the training, assistance and armament provided by the coalition."
With several powerful groups refusing to disarm, senior politicians have intervened and are now hoping to work out a compromise deal.
Factions have put forward conditions that include not only the withdrawal of foreign troops, but also an end to American political and economic interference.
The powerful Kataeb Hezbollah group said the withdrawal of "the occupation forces... is a start towards achieving full sovereignty."
But the group also threatened Zaidi's government.
"A government that doesn't work for the good of its people will be brought down by all possible means," it said.
Pro-Iran groups have long demanded the withdrawal of US troops and began targeting them with drones and missiles, triggering US retaliatory strikes that killed several faction commanders over the years.
During the Middle East war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran and allied factions intensified their attacks in Iraq, targeting US-led troops in the Kurdistan region.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SpaceX contributes 50 starlink kits to support Malaysia's disaster preparedness
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: United States Aerospace Company, SpaceX, donated 50 units of Starlink kits to Malaysia to support the country's disaster preparedness, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said the contribution was presented by a SpaceX delegation during a courtesy call at the Perdana Putra Building in Putrajaya, which was also attended by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Anwar said the meeting, among other things, discussed efforts to strengthen strategic cooperation through Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by the company, with a specific focus on expanding network access to residents in rural areas.
"I appreciate Starlink's role in supporting the government's efforts to expand coverage and improve the quality of internet access through the National Digital Network (Jendela), including in rural areas of Sabah and Sarawak as well as Orang Asli settlements in the Peninsula.
"I also welcome the operation of Starlink's Point of Presence (PoP) infrastructure in Cyberjaya to smoothen local data traffic and improve service quality for users," he said in a Facebook post.
At the same time, Anwar said technological advancement must bring tangible benefits to the people, alongside ensuring that cybersecurity, data protection, and safe internet usage continue to be given priority in tandem with the expansion of internet access.
"We want to ensure that communities in rural areas also enjoy quality and safe internet access so that they are not left behind in the country's current of progress," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Firefighters wade through floodwaters for 2km to rescue seven in Klang
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Firefighters waded through waist-deep floodwaters for two kilometres to rescue a family of seven, including four children, who were trapped by flash floods at Taman Rashna, Klang.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said firefighters had to make the journey on foot as the high water level prevented their fire engine from reaching the affected residential area.
He said the department received an emergency call around 7pm, prompting a team from the Klang Selatan Fire and Rescue Station to rush to the scene.
"The operations commander reported that the floodwaters were waist-deep, preventing the fire engine from entering the area due to the high water level.
[[nid:1544896]]
"Firefighters had to walk two kilometres to reach the affected residential area.
"All victims, including four children, were found and brought to safety," he said in a statement today.
Ashrul Riezal said the victims were taken to a safe elevated area, while the flash flood situation was showing signs of improvement.
Several areas around Shah Alam were earlier reported to have been hit by flash floods following heavy rain at about 4pm.
Checks on social media revealed that flash floods were reported around i-City in Section 7, the area near the rear entrance of Universiti Teknologi MARA, the Padang Jawa traffic light junction in Section 16 and the Bukit Raja traffic light intersection.
More recent posts reported flooding in other areas, including Taman Intan and Taman Rashna in Klang, Sungai Rasau and Section U12.
Roads around the affected areas remained congested as floodwaters had yet to fully recede.

Title: Passenger on rerouted flydubai flight says pilot tried to crash plane
Article:
TABUK, Saudi Arabia: A passenger on a rerouted flydubai flight that was bound for Tel Aviv said one of the pilots tried to crash the plane and kill everyone on board, after both pilots were found to be wounded on landing in Saudi Arabia.
In the first comment by an official, Israel's far-right national security minister Itamar Ben Gvir alleged an attempted "terrorist" attack in the incident, in which none of the passengers reported injuries.
The flydubai plane was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia's Tabuk "at 9.45am (0645 GMT) and its captain and copilot were found to have injuries and were transported to hospital", a statement from the company operating the airport said.
The low-cost carrier had earlier said flight FZ 1073 "experienced an incident while en route. The aircraft has landed safely in Tabuk Airport (TUU) and all passengers are safe and accounted for."
According to data from the Flightradar website, the aircraft suddenly lost altitude during the flight, dropping from nearly 34,000 feet at 0521 GMT to less than 17,000 feet at 0522 GMT.
Passenger Miryam Shira Ohayon said the plane was "pretty much out of control" when one of the pilots tried to stab the other while they were flying over Jordan en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
"So the co-pilot tried to murder the pilot and basically carry out a suicide attack on the plane," she told reporters by speakerphone held up by her mother who was waiting at Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv.
"It was really on the way to crashing, and it was simply the resourcefulness of many people who took control of the co-pilot and neutralised him," she said.
"There was also a doctor who gave first aid, and people who treated both of them. Other than the pilot, there were no injuries, but the bigger fear was really a crash, which is exactly what he was trying to do."
Several Israeli media reported that a fight had broken out between the plane's pilots, reportedly causing a distress signal to be activated.
Israeli media also reported that two other pilots were flying on the plane as passengers, and that they had taken over the controls to carry out the emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
At Ben Gurion airport, families gathered to await the return of their loved ones.
Earlier, Yasmin Abukasis, Ohayon's mother, told AFP her daughter called her from Saudi Arabia: "She said one pilot tried to kill the other pilot with a knife. They heard shouting."
Another passenger went to the cockpit "and saw a lot of blood. She started screaming 'come help' and some people went in and caught the guy", she added.
'GOING DOWN VERY FAST'
"All the while, the plane started going down very fast. People thought they were going to die."
She added that two other pilots in the back later took over the controls.
Neither the airline nor authorities of the countries involved provided details on what happened on board or on the pilots' nationalities, but some Israeli media said one was Omani and the other Emirati.
Israel's Kan public broadcaster and Channel 12 reported that the Israeli military had scrambled fighter jets after fears of a possible hijacking.
The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the premier had held consultations on the matter and was "monitoring developments."
Contacted by AFP, the Israeli military said it was "checking" the reports.
Meir Zohar, the father of passenger Ido Zohar, told AFP his son had told him by text message that he was well, but that he had no other news.
"We heard on the news what happened in the sky of Abu Dhabi," he said.
"He told us that everything is okay, he didn't tell me that much."
BLOODIED T-SHIRT
Israeli media, citing anonymous sources, reported that the passengers on board had stepped in to separate the two pilots during their altercation, publishing photos of a passenger with a bloodied T-shirt.
Channel 12 reported that authorities were investigating whether or not one of the pilots had attempted a possible suicide by trying to crash the plane, with the other pilot apparently intervening to prevent the crash.
An AFP correspondent in Tabuk, where the plane landed, saw heavy security near the airport, with several police vehicles and an ambulance parked at the terminal.
Access to the terminal remained open.
In photos sent to AFP by one of the passengers, travellers, including children, are seen gathered in an airport lounge, with some sitting on the floor, while one man is wearing a white T-shirt and jeans stained with blood.
The incident comes as tensions are high across the Middle East, amid the regional war that erupted in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran.
It also comes just ahead of close-fought Israeli elections due to be held at the end of October.
On Tuesday, Netanyahu said there were "indications" that Israel's enemies could try to attack ahead of elections, and was accused of "fear-mongering" by the opposition chief.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Motorcyclist wins hearts clearing drain in Johor Baru floods [WATCH]
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A motorcyclist braved fast-rising floodwaters to clear a blocked drain beneath the Taman Perling flyover in Johor Baru.
The man was seen walking through floodwater along Jalan Skudai beneath the flyover after heavy rain caused flash floods in several parts of the city.
Footage recorded by a passing motorist showed him clearing rubbish and debris from the drain before it was shared on social media.
Several netizens praised the man, saying his actions helped clear the obstruction and allowed the stagnant floodwater to drain more quickly.

Title: Housewife's RM6,000 'Immigration officer' act busted
Article:
AYER KEROH: A housewife in her 50s allegedly charged RM6,000 per client by posing as a senior immigration department officer and offering to arrange work permits for foreigners.
Her activities, believed to have been ongoing for one to two years, were uncovered after she was arrested while allegedly arranging a Temporary Employment Visit Pass (PLKS) application for a Chinese national at a cafe in Taman Malim Jaya around 6pm yesterday.
Melaka Immigration director Anirwan Fauzee Mohd Aini said the woman was arrested following a complaint and intelligence gathering by the department's enforcement division.
"The suspect is believed to have posed as a senior immigration director at the headquarters and the immigration department's integrity chief.
"She allegedly charged RM6,000 for each person seeking her services and offered to arrange work permit applications without clients, particularly foreigners, having to visit the Immigration office.
"At the time of her arrest, she was with a client believed to have sought her services," he said at a press conference at the Home Ministry Complex.
Anirwan said the first raid was conducted outside a cafe in Taman Malim Jaya, followed by a second raid at a condominium in Taman Kota Laksamana.
Various items believed to have been used to convince clients of her purported identity as an Immigration officer were seized from her home and vehicle.
They included a black immigration uniform with accessories, senior officer rank insignia, a collar badge, integrity and Setia Berjasa badges, black work shoes, two immigration-logo T-shirts, a suspected fake immigration identification card, a name stamp and an approval letter bearing the department's letterhead.
"The suspect had never worked with the department. She is a housewife with five children," he said.
Anirwan said the woman was believed to have operated from different locations in Melaka and had no fixed base to avoid detection.
She also used social media, including posting photographs of herself wearing an Immigration uniform, to convince potential clients of her identity.
"We are investigating how she obtained the department's uniform and accessories and whether other parties were involved," he said.
The case is being investigated under Sections 56(1)(k) and 56(1)(l) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
The woman was remanded for four days by the Alor Gajah Sessions Court from today to assist investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zetrix, IPVG extend RM130mil MyEG Ventures deal deadline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd and IPVG Employees Inc have extended the deadline by three months to complete the former's acquisition of a 50 per cent stake in Philippines-based MyEG Ventures Inc.
Zetrix AI said both parties agreed to complete the share purchase agreement by the end of the fourth quarter, instead of the original deadline of Wednesday.
Zetrix AI said the extension mainly allows more time to fulfil the conditions precedent under the agreement.
The RM130 million deal marks the company's second attempt to acquire the stake in MyEG Ventures.
On Sept 1, Zetrix AI agreed to buy the 50 per cent stake from Next Lion Ltd, whose sole shareholder and director is Yap Shon Leong.
However, it terminated the agreement three days later after reviewing the commercial rationale amid volatility in the price of the consideration shares.
The termination followed two rounds of queries from Bursa Malaysia, with neither party required to pay a break fee.
Zetrix AI later said the deal fell through over a dispute on the issue price of the consideration shares.
It signed the new agreement with IPVG Employees on Sept 4 and announced it on Sept 7.
IPVG Employees, led by Filipino entrepreneur Jaime Enrique Y Gonzalez, currently owns 9.4 per cent of MyEG Ventures.
It will acquire another 40.6 per cent from IP Ventures Inc, Shennan A Sy, Edward Derrick P Chiongbian and Kaikaku Fund LP before selling the resulting 50 per cent stake to Zetrix AI.
If completed, Zetrix AI's effective interest in MYEG Philippines will rise to 74.5 per cent from 49 per cent, allowing it to consolidate the business as a subsidiary.
Zetrix AI said it will only pay for the stake after all conditions are fulfilled, including the registration of the 50 per cent interest in its name.
Bursa Malaysia questioned the valuation of MYEG Philippines in a third round of queries on Sept 8.
MYEG Philippines recorded an average annual net profit of 21.6 million pesos (about RM1.4 million) for the three financial years ended 2025, while its net assets stood at about RM20 million at end-2025.
Zetrix AI had said IPVG was expected to complete its purchase of the remaining 40.6 per cent by the end of the third quarter of 2026.
The latest extension comes after a sharp sell-off in Zetrix AI shares.
The stock lost about two-thirds of its market capitalisation between Aug 27 and Sept 2, when it hit a 12-year low of 22 sen following a margin call involving managing director Wong Thean Soon.
Wong now holds a 6.1 per cent direct stake and a 4.78 per cent indirect interest in the company.

Title: MLFF implementation not to be rushed – Nanta
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The implementation of the Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) tolling system will not be rushed, with stakeholders given more time to finalise the arrangements, said Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi.
He said the parties involved had been given a timeline to work out the details, with several platforms already being considered, although negotiations were still ongoing.
"We have given them a timeline. They just need a little bit more time, and there are platforms that they have already also thought of.
"I do not want to reveal for the time being because it is still under negotiation," he said at a press conference after the opening ceremony of the MyAsean Road and Traffic Tech Expo 2026 here today.
Nanta said the implementation would follow a business-to-business (B2B) model, with highway concessionaires and other interested parties working together to develop the system.
Nanta said the approach would allow interested parties to negotiate among themselves, particularly highway concessionaires, which own the highways and related assets.
"We did not do this in a rush, and all these years and months have been used to ensure that those parties who are coming together, as we allow it on a B2B model. Meaning to say, people interested in implementing this, if they want, they must talk among each other, especially the concessionaires," he said.
He said the highway association also played an important role in facilitating negotiations between concessionaires and other parties interested in investing in the system.
Commenting on payment integration across different highways, Nanta highlighted the ongoing pilot testing of the 'JustGo' system on selected expressways, including those operated by Plus Malaysia Berhad.
"The JustGo system currently in use serves as an introduction or pilot project. Under the B2B framework, participating parties will evaluate whether the JustGo platform or alternative platforms can be adopted collaboratively across networks," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Batu Kawan clears 95pct in MKH takeover
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Batu Kawan Bhd's unconditional mandatory takeover of MKH Bhd has crossed the 95 per cent threshold, paving the way for the property developer to be delisted from Bursa Malaysia.
As at market close on Wednesday, Batu Kawan and its wholly owned unit Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd, together with parties acting in concert, held 548.85 million MKH shares.
This represents a 95.16 per cent stake, according to a statement issued on their behalf by Maybank Investment Bank Bhd.
With valid acceptances received for not less than nine-tenths in nominal value of the offer shares, Batu Kawan and Whitmore will invoke Section 222(1) of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 to compulsorily buy the remaining MKH shares from dissenting shareholders.
The takeover offer will remain open until Oct 8, following an extension from the original Sept 17 closing date.
Bursa Malaysia will suspend trading in MKH shares five market days from Oct 8.
Thereafter, Batu Kawan and Whitmore will procure MKH to take the necessary steps to withdraw its listing status.

Title: RM100mil spent on JB flood mitigation, but system overwhelmed by intense rain
Article:
JOHOR BARU: More than RM100 million has been spent by the city council on drainage and flood mitigation works since 2023, but existing infrastructure was still unable to fully cope with today's intense rainfall coinciding with a high tide.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said rainfall intensity reached 60mm an hour, three times the reference rate of 20mm an hour, while the high tide reached 3.5 metres.
He said the combination placed significant pressure on the city's drainage and flood mitigation systems.
"However, today's incident shows that existing infrastructure is still unable to fully cope with the flow load when high-intensity rainfall occurs simultaneously with a high tide," he said in a statement today.
Jafni said rainfall between 1pm and 7pm totalled about 90mm, with rainfall increasing significantly between 1.30pm and 5pm.
He said the high concentration of rain within a short period caused a sharp increase in water flow, placing pressure on drainage and retention systems.
"The high sea level also raises the downstream water level and reduces the difference in levels needed for water to be discharged by gravity.
"This can cause a backwater effect, slowing drainage flow and raising water levels upstream," he said.
Jafni said rapid development had also increased paved and built-up areas, reducing water infiltration into the ground and accelerating surface runoff into the drainage network.
He said the capacity of the drainage system therefore needed to be assessed based on the entire catchment area and its ability to handle peak flows.
Jafni inspected six locations today, including Ayer Molek, the area near the Tabung Haji office, Kampung Mohd Amin, the pumping station in front of Dataran Bandaraya, Jalan Danga opposite Tune Hotel and surrounding areas.
The inspection focused on retention capacity, peak-flow drainage capacity, outlet conditions and pumping operations to discharge water into the Johor Strait.
For 2027, RM46.8 million has been allocated specifically for flood management, with priorities to be determined based on technical assessments of drainage, retention and pumping capacity, flood risk in each catchment and the impact of tides on water discharge into the Johor Strait.
At Kampung Mohd Amin, Jafni said the retention pond would be deepened to increase its effective storage capacity and accommodate more water during peak flows.
He said technical assessments would also take into account the pond's base level, silt accumulation, bank stability and the levels of inlet and outlet structures.
At Jalan Danga opposite Tune Hotel, the on-site detention (OSD) facility would be upgraded to increase temporary storage and regulate discharge into the main drainage system.
He said the OSD facility near Tabung Haji would also be assessed, including its inlet and outlet conditions and the possibility of flow obstruction caused by silt, rubbish or high downstream water levels.
Jafni said the number of pumps used to discharge water from Johor Baru city centre into the Johor Strait had been increased from four to eight units.
However, he said the pumping system's performance needed to be assessed based on actual flow rates and operating conditions, including pumping height, energy losses in pipelines, inlet capacity, power supply, standby pumps and water-level activation controls.
He said affected areas also included squatter settlements, private land and locations under the maintenance responsibility of different parties.
"Water flows across land ownership boundaries. Therefore, assessments need to cover the continuity of drainage from upstream to downstream, including drainage connections, culverts, flow obstructions and maintenance access," he said.
Jafni said cooperation between local authorities, technical agencies and landowners was crucial to ensure measures taken at one location did not increase the risk of flooding elsewhere.
He said he had also directed the city council to provide immediate assistance and coordinate technical and safety inspections following a landslide at Pangsapuri Saujana caused by the heavy rain.
The assessment would cover slope stability, soil saturation, surface and underground drainage conditions and signs of ground movement, he said.
Jafni said he would chair the Johor Baru Flood Task Force meeting tomorrow involving local authorities and relevant technical agencies.
He said the meeting would examine rainfall data, tide records, the level and duration of inundation, drainage capacity and pump-operation records.
"These findings will form the basis for identifying locations that restrict water flow, determining immediate measures and prioritising upgrading works, complete with lead agencies, implementation timelines and monitoring," he said.
Jafni said all local authorities and relevant agencies had been directed to take immediate action at locations affected by
flash floods.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore launches dating service for public servants
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore has launched a dating platform for public officials, in the city-state's latest experiment meant to tackle declining marriage and historically low fertility rates.
The algorithm-powered pilot initiative, unveiled on Tuesday and named FirstDate, targets employees aged between 21 to 35 and promises to end "swipe fatigue", associated with some dating apps, while building a "thoughtful connection."
Public officials can fill out details including interests, habits, religious preferences and "dealbreakers."
The platform promises absolute privacy, saying "only your match sees your profile, and you decide if your contact details are shared."
It does, however, also ask users to "Tell us how your date went!" with a star rating and an optional feedback box.
Applications to take part in the pilot close on Monday.
Singapore, which has a population of just over six million people, saw record-low fertility rates last year.
Fewer Singaporeans are getting married, with official figures showing that marriage registrations fell for the third consecutive year in 2025.
In August, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced a robust package encouraging larger families, including generous financial incentives.
Singapore also officially became a super-aged society this year, where at least 21 percent of the population is aged 65 and above.
In Japan, an AI-powered dating app launched by the Tokyo government in 2024 to lift Japan's low birthrate led to 265 marriages. — AFP

Title: Rejoining EU among options for future ties - UK PM
Article:
LONDON: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in an interview broadcast Wednesday that rejoining the EU was among the potential answers to the unavoidable question of what Britain's future relationship with Europe could look like.
His comments came after he told his ruling Labour Party's annual conference that he would set out "different options" for future ties with the European Union closer to a planned summit with the bloc later this year.
Britain voted to leave the bloc in the contentious 2016 Brexit referendum.
Burnham, who campaigned to stay in the EU, has previously said he hoped Britain would return to the 27-nation bloc within his lifetime.
Options that could be looked at now included joining the European single market and customs union, "or we could go all the way", he told BBC Radio's Today Programme.
"So there are clearly options that need to be considered, and we have to look at what is doable, and what would be the pros and cons of each.
"What I am saying is it's not good enough to leave that question just hanging," he said.
Burnham, who has been prime minister since July, told the Labour conference in his leader's speech that Brexit had triggered "a decade of low growth which has put us in a weaker position."
"We will not give Britain the clear path we need into the rest of this century until we decide on a long-term relationship with what is still our largest market," he added in the speech Tuesday.
The summit with the bloc had been due to be held in July in Brussels.
But that plan was derailed when former prime minister Keir Starmer was ousted as Labour leader and replaced by Burnham.
The Financial Times reported Wednesday that November 20 had now been pencilled in for the summit, although the date has not been confirmed.
The two sides had been hoping to present several deals at the summit, namely on food and animal safety standards, a youth mobility scheme and the linking of their emissions-trading systems.

Title: Five charged over alleged false documents in hardcore poor house repairs
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A civil servant and four company owners were charged in the Special Corruption Court here today over alleged offences involving repair works on houses under the Hardcore Poor Housing Programme (PPRT).
They are Sabah Agriculture Department administrative assistant Aidah Mustapha, 54, and company owners Ashar Usman, 45; Shariff Wahya, 55; Kenidi Musa, 41; and Mohd Nur Musa, 42.
All five pleaded not guilty to their respective charges before Sessions Court Judge Andi Razalijaya A Dadi.
The offences were allegedly committed between February and September 2021 at the Sabah GiatMara office here.
Aidah faces 10 charges, while Kenidi and Mohd Nur face five charges each. Ashar and Shariff face one charge each.
Four of the charges against Aidah involve submitting invoices containing false documents to the then Sabah GiatMara director in relation to repair works on PPRT houses for several recipients.
According to the charges, the repair works did not comply with the stipulated work specifications.
The offences under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 and punishable under Section 24(1) of the Act provides for a jail term of up to 20 years, and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the gratification, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
The remaining six charges against Aidah involve using false documents as genuine to deceive and obtain payment for the repair works.
The documents included Certificates of Work Completion and Handover, PPRT application forms under the People's Welfare Development Scheme (SPKR), consent forms for the use of privately owned land for PPRT projects, PPRT recipient verification and declaration forms, and PPRT participant profile forms.
The offences, under Section 471 of the Penal Code and punishable under Section 465 of the same Code, carry a jail term of up to two years, a fine, or both.
Meanwhile, the four other accused were charged with submitting documents containing false statements relating to PPRT house repair works to the then Sabah GiatMara director.
Each charge involved a PPRT house where the repair works were either not carried out or did not comply with the stipulated work specifications.
The court fixed Oct 28 for case management.
All five accused were granted bail in varying amounts, with between one and two local sureties each.
The court also ordered them to report to the nearest MACC office once a month, surrender their international and/or restricted passports to the court and refrain from approaching prosecution witnesses.
MACC prosecuting officer Dzulkarnain Rousan Hasbi prosecuted, while Aidah was represented by lawyer Jessica Ombou.
The other four accused were unrepresented.

Title: Astro slips into RM25.8mil net loss in Q2
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Astro Malaysia Holdings Bhd slipped into a net loss in the second quarter ended July 31, 2026 with a net loss of RM25.80 million, compared with a net profit of RM16.39 million a year ago.
This was  weighed by unrealised foreign exchange losses on unhedged transponder lease liabilities following the weaker ringgit, Astro said in its filing with Bursa Malaysia.
Revenue fell 7.2 per cent to RM633.75 million from RM683.21 million, mainly due to lower contributions from its subscription and advertising businesses.
Revenue from its television segment fell RM49 million, or 7.5 per cent, to RM606 million from RM655 million in the corresponding quarter, while radio revenue declined marginally by RM0.4 million, or 1.4 per cent.
The group did not declare a dividend for the quarter.
Astro interim group chief executive officer Henry Tan said the company is focused on building a stronger and more future-ready business by expanding its audience, deepening engagement and developing new revenue streams.
"This journey is underway and our direction is clear: reach more Malaysians, create greater value from our content and customer engagement, and build new revenue opportunities across streaming, advertising and adjacent businesses," he said.

Title: Johari vows to address Titiwangsa residents' concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Titiwangsa member of parliament Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani has pledged to address concerns raised by residents in the constituency, including on the lack of suitable recreational facilities for children.
Johari, who is also investment, trade and industry minister, said he was open to meeting joint management bodies (JMBs) and management corporations (MC) in his constituency to discuss issues affecting residents.
"I am always open to receiving invitations from any JMB or MC of apartments or condominiums in the Titiwangsa parliamentary constituency, particularly on issues that can be discussed to help residents," he said in a Facebook post.
He said this after meeting residents of Residensi Pandanmas 2 in Kampung Pandan here, following an invitation from its JMB.

Title: Divfex secures RM120mil data centre equipment supply contracts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Divfex Bhd (DFX) has secured two separate supply agreements worth a combined RM120.12 million for the procurement and supply of key equipments for a 15-megawatt (MW) data centre fit-out in Penang.
The company said its wholly owned subsidiary, Diversified Gateway Bhd (DGB), and its 51 per cent-owned subsidiary, Excel Commerce Solutions Sdn Bhd (EXCEL), signed the agreements with a leading Malaysian-incorporated data centre company involved in the provision of data centre facility services and related infrastructure today.
Under the first supply agreement, DGB would supply generator sets, transformers, switchgear and low-voltage equipment for RM84.44 million, while EXCEL would supply cables under the second agreement for RM35.67 million.
"Delivery under the supply agreements are expected to be completed within three months from the first delivery, subject to an extension of up to six months by mutual agreement in writing," it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
Barring any unforeseen circumstances, it said the supply agreements are expected to contribute positively towards the revenue, future earnings and net assets of DFX Group for the financial year ending June 30, 2027.
The company said there were no foreseeable significant risks other than operational, procurement, delivery and counterparty payment risks associated with the supply agreements during the project duration.

Title: UWC FY26 net profit jumps to RM93.83mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: UWC Bhd's net profit jumped to RM93.83 million in the financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY26) from RM40.51 million a year ago.
The engineering services company said its revenue also increased to RM594.89 million compared with RM386.17 million previously.
For the fourth quarter ended July 31, 2026, UWC recorded a higher net profit of RM37.59 million from RM16.36 million, while revenue rose to RM186.17 million from RM108.79 million previously.
"The higher revenue was supported by stronger semiconductor demand, the progressive execution of secured frontend semiconductor projects and increased demand for back-end semiconductor equipment," it said in a Bursa Malaysia filing.
UWC said it also reflected the group's strategic expansion into higher-precision, mission-critical and value-added contract manufacturing, extending its scope from individual component manufacturing to the delivery of more complex modules, sub-systems and integrated assemblies.
On outlook, the group remains cautiously optimistic about its business outlook, supported by the continued strength of the semiconductor industry, increasing demand from both front-end and back-end semiconductor customers, and the progressive ramp-up of recently secured projects and new product introductions.

Title: Anwar hails UM for breaking into world top 200
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Universiti Malaya (UM) on becoming the first Malaysian university to break into the top 200 of the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2027.
He said UM's ranking of 194th in the list reflected the university's excellence in teaching and research.
Anwar said the achievement also instilled confidence that local higher education institutions were capable of competing with leading universities worldwide.
"Hence, this excellence must continue to be strengthened through a thriving culture of knowledge, freedom of thought and research that addresses the needs of society and the country.
"Universities must produce a generation that is sharp-minded, steadfast in values and morals, and courageous in exploring new ideas.
"This achievement should serve as a catalyst for Universiti Malaya and all our higher education institutions to continue improving quality and elevating the standing of knowledge," he said in a Facebook post.
Anwar also expressed hope that UM would continue to achieve successes that would bring honour to Malaysia.

Title: Five remanded after fake gold bracelet pawned in Johor
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Five suspects, including a foreign woman, have been remanded for three days after a bracelet pawned at a pawnshop in Sungai Rengit was found to be fake.
District police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the three men, a local woman and the foreigner, aged between 34 and 62, were arrested in Sungai Rengit between 1pm and 3pm yesterday.
The suspects were brought before the Pengerang magistrate's court and remanded from Sept 30 to Oct 2 to facilitate investigations under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
The case came to light after the pawnshop manager lodged a police report that the 23-gram bracelet was not gold.
Police did not disclose the amount paid, but a genuine 23-gram 916 gold bracelet could be worth around RM12,000.
One of the suspects had a previous crime linked to selling fake gold in Alor Star, while two others had previous narcotics offences.
Yusof said police believed the arrests could assist investigations into several cases involving the pawning or sale of fake gold in the district.

Title: Malaysia Airlines advises extra travel time to KLIA during F1 weekend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines has advised passengers travelling through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) between Oct 2 and 4 to allow extra time for their journey due to expected traffic congestion during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix Malaysia 2026.
The national carrier said congestion was expected in areas surrounding KLIA and on roads leading to the airport due to the event at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
"While access to KLIA remains available, passengers are advised to monitor the latest traffic and road closure updates from the police and plan alternative routes where necessary," it said in a statement.

It advised passengers to arrive at KLIA at least three hours before the scheduled departure time for international flights, and two hours before for domestic flights, to ensure a smooth process.

Title: SME association welcomes minimum wage increment exemption
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's decision to exempt small and medium enterprises (SMEs) from further minimum wage increases will protect 1.3 million SMEs nationwide, said the Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta).
Its national president Datuk William Ng welcomed the
cabinet decision
, which he said would help SMEs cope with rising costs, compressed margins and global economic uncertainties.
He said the move demonstrated the government's responsiveness to the challenges faced by SMEs while ensuring workers' welfare remained protected.
"Sustainable wage growth must be anchored on value creation and productivity gains. In this regard, we strongly endorse the government's strategic focus on the Progressive Wage Policy as the right way forward.
"By supporting productivity growth at both the firm and workers levels, we will be able to share prosperity more equitably between employers and workers," Ng said in a statement.
He urged the government to work with industry associations to provide rapid SME-focused training programmes to help businesses improve productivity.
At the same time, Samenta said wage policy should not be viewed in isolation, with the government needing to address structural costs faced by SMEs.
These include compliance and regulatory costs, logistics and utility expenses, as well as access to low-interest working capital financing, Ng said.
Despite welcoming the exemption, Samenta urged SMEs that could afford to pay higher wages to do so to retain talent and build a more motivated workforce.
Ng said Samenta remained committed to working with the Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Ministry, Human Resources Ministry and other relevant ministries to help SMEs transition into higher-productivity and higher-value businesses capable of offering competitive wages.

Title: RON97, RON95 prices down 5 sen, diesel 15 sen from Oct 1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Retail prices of unsubsidised RON97 and RON95 petrol will fall by 5 sen per litre, while unsubsidised diesel will drop by 15 sen per litre from Oct 1 to 7.
The Finance Ministry (MoF) said the new prices would be RM5 per litre for RON97, RM4.52 per litre for unsubsidised RON95 and RM5.27 per litre for unsubsidised diesel.
In a statement, it said the reduction was driven by moderating average global crude oil prices during the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period, following the resumption of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline operations.
"At the same time, the supply of refined petroleum products in Asia is showing signs of recovery, with China's refined petroleum product exports in September estimated to exceed four million tonnes, compared with an average of around three million tonnes per month last year.
"This increase in supply helps to reduce part of the pressure on regional petroleum product prices," it said.
However, the ministry said the recovery in global supply remained uneven, with another major Russian refinery in Perm forced to halt operations following a Ukrainian drone attack last week, limiting Russian diesel supplies to the international market.
It said volatility in petroleum product prices was expected to persist as long as the conflict between the United States and Iran remained unresolved.
"Any new attacks in the Middle East risk placing upward pressure on oil and petroleum product prices once again.
"Furthermore, the recovery of global refining capacity remains crucial to easing price pressures in the medium term," it said.
MoF said the Madani government would continue to protect the people and businesses from the impact of global volatility, including by maintaining targeted subsidies through Budi Madani, Budi Diesel, the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS).
At the current prices, Budi95 recipients pay RM1.99 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised RON95 price of RM4.52 per litre.
The government bears a subsidy of RM2.53 per litre, equivalent to 56 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
"Budi Diesel recipients will continue to pay RM2.10 per litre compared with the unsubsidised diesel price of RM5.27 per litre, with a government subsidy of RM3.17 per litre or 60 per cent of the unsubsidised price," it said.

Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 – Firemen managed to rescue 37 pupils and seven teachers who were earlier trapped in the Umiku Sayang Kindergarten and Nursery on Jalan Muhd Amin here after it was inundated by a flash floods today.
Larkin Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Nakish Nekmat said that authorities received an distress call regarding the incident at 3.53pm.
Following the call, a team of 10 firemen – equipped with a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit – were dispatched to the scene that was located about 10 kilometres away.

Title: Ex-EPF CEO proposes employers pay higher EPF contributions for low-wage workers while reducing contributions for high-income staff
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — To help lower-salary workers save up more money for their retirement through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), their employers could help put in more money towards their EPF savings, former EPF CEO Tan Sri Shahril Ridza Ridzuan said today.
Shahril, currently Axiata Group Berhad’s chairman, noted that Malaysia currently has one of the highest contribution rates from employees and their employers for retirement savings in EPF.
Currently in Malaysia, the law requires Malaysian employees below age 60 to contribute 11 per cent of their salary into their EPF retirement savings, while employers will have to contribute 13 per cent of the salary (if the employee’s salary is below RM5,000) or 12 per cent (if above RM5,000).
“So the contribution rate itself is not the problem. The problem has always been for the last 50, 60 years, the fact really that wages have not grown fast enough in Malaysia. So when your base is small, no matter how big your contribution rate, you are just not building your retirement savings fast enough,” he said as a speaker at EPF’s International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 here titled “The Long Horizon”.
He commended the current federal government for its efforts on working towards having a progressive wage policy to make sure workers get a fair share of the economy: “And we need to continue that. We need to have much better progressive policies to make sure that the minimum wage keeps going up.”
Later, Shahril suggested that a progressive wage policy would not just cover workers’ income levels, and proposed that it be used to set policies on EPF contribution rates from employers.
“And I would actually propose and suggest basically that employers pay a much higher contribution rate for workers below a certain threshold, and compensated really by then having a much lower contribution rate for workers past the threshold.
“So for instance, if you are earning below RM5,000, why shouldn’t employers contribute say 15 per cent or 16 per cent to your EPF?
“That helps basically in terms of building your retirement savings. It’s progressive in the sense of basically allowing for lower-income workers to build their savings faster,” he said.
“But you can then compensate by saying, for instance, that any worker above, for instance RM10,000, employers should only contribute four per cent,” he said when giving a hypothetical example to illustrate his point.
He said this would also help to cap the amount of money that EPF manages for high-income workers, such as those who are already earning RM10,000 and if they are well on their way to achieving their financial retirement plans.
He said this would be a better method than the hypothetical method of giving different investment yields for those with lower and higher total EPF savings.
“So instead of basically differentiating between account yields for those with higher balances in EPF and lower balances, actually what you should do is to start capping this contributions of high-income earners to reduce the size of their balance sheet,” he said in giving his proposed solution.
Shahril was responding to a question on how lower-income workers and informal workers can also achieve a dignified retirement through their retirement savings.
Currently in Malaysia, the law requires Malaysian employees below age 60 to contribute 11 per cent of their salary into their EPF retirement savings, while employers will have to contribute 13 per cent of the salary (if the employee’s salary is below RM5,000) or 12 per cent (if above RM5,000). — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Earlier during his session, Shahril said he believed that having differentiated yields for EPF accounts will never be the right solution, as the EPF base is too big in terms of the number of EPF contributors it has.
He also said introducing differentiated yields on EPF accounts would carry a “very high risk” of outflow of funds from top EPF account holders.
He said this hypothetical scenario leading to funds outflow would be bad for all EPF members, as part of the reason for EPF’s success is that a bigger Assets Under Management (AUM) or total assets managed would translate to lower cost for all.
Shahril said the actual debate should be about improving wealth inequality in Malaysia and a better transfer of wealth between capital owners and workers: “So the fight is not really about between whether you are high-wage earner or whether you are low-wage earner. It’s really between, are you an owner of capital and business, and whether you are essentially paying a fair share to the state in order to support these policies.”
Gig workers
As for gig workers, Shahril said they face an “invisible tax” as gig platforms do not contribute to EPF savings towards those working on their platforms, which means the platforms have a lower operating cost and can then outcompete traditional brick-and-mortar businesses and Mom-and-Pop stores.
He proposed that a revenue tax be imposed on gig platforms, and that the money raised from this tax could then be used to provide for EPF contributions for gig workers.
“So I think there are ways of doing it right? It’s just a matter of being creative around understanding the maths and understanding how to push those boundaries for the betterment of those workers and those gig workers who are probably under-covered at this point in time,” he said.
